correctness.rationale: C PASS. The Petersen graph is represented canonically as KG(5,2), with 10 vertices, 15 undirected edges and exactly 2^15=32768 complete bit-mask orientations. The packaged verifier checks all masks with Kahn peeling and a separate depth-first cycle detector, giving 16680 acyclic states (independently agreeing with the published chromatic polynomial at -1). It generates precisely the legal source/sink single-vertex flips, verifies acyclicity and adjacency reversal of all edges, then enumerates every click component. A BFS rooted at EVERY one of 16680 states visits its entire component and gives all pair distances. Independently for each reachable ordered pair, the potential-median formula of the published general theorem reproduces the BFS distance. The component size histogram sums to all 16680 states; the pair histogram sums to the exact component binomial sum 235080. All 120 induced S5 automorphisms are constructed and applied to component IDs; their nine orbits are exhaustively enumerated. The separate known 168 S5 orbits on individual orientations and 704 orientations with specified unique source are independently checked. The reversal claim is verified by flipping all 15 bits for representative orientations. These are complete finite computations, not extrapolations.

value.rationale: V PASS. The graph is the canonical nonbipartite cubic Petersen graph; source/sink conversions are a long-studied natural equivalence of acyclic orientations, with direct connections to Coxeter conjugacy and toric posets. The Tutte polynomial counts classes but loses all internal metric and symmetry information. The exact component-size/diameter census and complete S5 orbit decomposition recover previously unspecified geometric and representation data; especially, two twenty-one-state component families are indistinguishable by size, degree and distance statistics but are inequivalent under Aut(P) and are exchanged by global reversal. This is a natural finite exact classification of a motivated object, not an arbitrary slice or trivial restatement of a known coefficient.
